title: Align herbivore feeding targets with reproduction energy requirements
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem
Follow-up to gocreatures-007. Herbivores eat only at <=40% nutrition while reproduction requires roughly 70%. With maxNutrition=500, eating at 200 adds at most 100, reaching only 60%, after which feeding stops. This code-derived mismatch can prevent resource-rich animals from building breeding reserves; reproduce it with a deterministic scenario before changing policy. The reported tick 614 has one herbivore remaining and abundant vegetation; its Clones=0 is per-tick, not cumulative evidence of no herbivore births.

## Implementation
Introduce a documented breeding-reserve feeding target, initially evaluate 80–90% nutrition, coordinated with clone energy requirements. Permit food seeking and eating above the current 40% threshold when building that reserve. Ensure feeding priority does not postpone cloning indefinitely once reserves are sufficient. Preserve urgent hunger/escape behavior, offspring energy transfer, health/age eligibility, and cooldowns. Inspect actions.go canReproduce, decideHerbivoreAction, and decideAction; update domain documentation.

## Validation
Add a deterministic resource-rich mature-herbivore scenario demonstrating reserve accumulation and reproduction through normal ticks. Compare seeded population/reproduction outcomes with the existing baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduce the feeding/reproduction threshold mismatch in a deterministic regression test.
- A healthy mature herbivore with maxNutrition=500 and accessible sufficient food can build the required reserve and reproduce through normal decisions.
- Feeding targets and breeding thresholds are documented and cannot create a feed-versus-clone priority deadlock.
- Nutrition caps, finite food consumption, parental energy costs, and cooldowns remain respected.
- Relevant hunger/avoidance regressions, go test ./..., go test -race ./..., and go vet ./... pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Limit herbivore grazing to needed nutrition
description: Herbivores currently remove up to five plant biomass units per eat action, even when the resulting nutrition exceeds their remaining capacity. Excess nutrition is discarded while the plants are still depleted. Cap biomass consumed by the herbivore's remaining nutrition capacity, accounting for each selected plant's nutritional yield, before mutating biomass. Preserve species-yield preference and correct fractional nutrition handling. Add focused regression coverage and compare seeded ecology trajectories before/after.
acceptance_criteria: An herbivore at or near nutrition capacity does not remove biomass whose nutrition it cannot use; consumption remains bounded by the existing per-action limit and available biomass; species consumption and nutrition statistics remain correct; focused tests and go test ./... pass.
close_reason: Capped plant biomass consumption by remaining nutrition capacity; focused regressions pass.

title: Tune herbivore reproduction cooldown against plant demand
description: Test a modest increase to the herbivore clone cooldown (for example, from 20 to 30 or 40 ticks) to reduce herbivore population growth and plant pressure without changing carnivore reproduction. Keep the cooldown configurable through the existing rule/constants pattern, compare one value at a time over multiple fixed seeds and long runs, and document population, births, deaths, plant biomass/occupancy, and consumption-versus-growth outcomes. Select a value based on those diagnostics rather than a single run.
acceptance_criteria: Herbivore cooldown can be tuned independently from carnivores; regression coverage verifies the diet-specific cooldown; seeded multi-world diagnostics report relevant reproduction and plant metrics and are repeatable; go test ./... passes.

title: Protect plant regrowth from grazing extirpation
description: Plant colonies regrow only while biomass remains, and grazing a colony to zero clears its living cohort. Newly spread colonies lack dormant recovery reserves, so a grazing event can remove the local source of future regrowth. Explore and implement a small protected root/reserve biomass or equivalent recovery mechanism that lets depleted colonies recover without making inaccessible biomass edible or violating shared cell capacity. Cover grazing-to-zero and recovery behavior with deterministic tests; evaluate plant occupancy and biomass in seeded long-run ecology runs.
acceptance_criteria: A colony depleted by grazing can recover through the chosen explicit mechanism; protected/reserve biomass is not counted as edible biomass; cell capacity and biomass accounting invariants hold; deterministic tests and go test ./... pass.

title: Recover depleted plants only at original seed locations
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Goal
Implement proposal item 2: a plant recovery mechanism that buffers temporary overgrazing. User constraint: recovery applies only to original plant seed locations.

## Scope and semantics
Treat original seed locations as species/location pairs receiving positive biomass during world initialization, including patch centers and their initially seeded cardinal halos. Track eligibility independently for grass, clover, and bramble. Later spread, mutation, or recolonization must never create additional recovery locations. Preserve founder-location metadata independently of living colony state so grazing a colony to zero cannot erase it.

Introduce protected roots or a finite dormant seed reserve at those locations. After edible biomass reaches zero, allow delayed recovery only when reserve and shared cell capacity permit it. Recovery must consume a documented reserve budget; sustained repeated depletion can exhaust that budget. Choose and document recovery delay, reserve size, biomass per recovery, and whether/how reserves replenish. Do not replenish an exhausted reserve automatically without an explicit ecological rule. At other locations, a lost colony requires ordinary spread to return.

Define recovered cohort traits and generation explicitly, distinguishing dormant recovery from daughter establishment. A species may recover after all its living biomass disappears if eligible dormant reserves remain. Dormant reserves are not edible biomass and must not count as occupied living colonies. Existing shared capacity and snapshot/no-same-tick-spread-cascade semantics must remain valid.

## Implementation context
main.go seedPlants seeds centers and halos, scaling overlapping species to shared capacity. plantPopulation, PlantCellAt, updatePlants, regrowPlants, and actions.go resolveEat are relevant entry points. Colony clearing currently discards living cohort state; recovery eligibility must survive it. Update PLANTS.md and CONTEXT.md, whose current contract says zero-biomass colonies never spontaneously return.

## Reporting and validation
Expose recovery events and biomass separately from spread transfers and ordinary regrowth, with a documented mass-balance relationship to total biomass added. Use deterministic scenarios to validate recovery eligibility, delay, capacity, reserve exhaustion, and species-specific behavior. Compare seeded long-run vegetation persistence and creature coexistence against baseline without claiming guaranteed equilibrium.
acceptance_criteria:
- Initialization records recovery eligibility only for species/location pairs with positive founding biomass, including centers and halos.
- Complete grazing at an eligible site can recover after the configured delay with available reserve/capacity; identical depletion at a later spread site cannot recover without incoming spread.
- Recovery permission never propagates with descendants or mutations and never enables another unseeded species in the same cell.
- Dormant metadata survives clearing and recolonization; repeated depletion cannot bypass the documented reserve budget or delay.
- Recovery respects shared capacity, has no same-tick spread cascade, and uses documented trait/generation semantics.
- Reporting distinguishes recovery, regrowth, and transfer without double-counting biomass or living occupancy.
- Deterministic tests cover overlapping initial patches, species-specific eligibility, exhaustion, full cells, and recovery after live-species extinction.
- Documentation, seeded baseline comparison, go test ./..., go test -race ./..., and go vet ./... are completed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace hard local-food reproduction vetoes with gradual breeding probability
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem
Follow-up to gocreatures-007. canReproduce requires local plant energy per herbivore >=6 times maxNutrition, or local prey energy per carnivore >=0.5 times maxNutrition. These binary gates may suppress replacement even when parents have adequate stored energy. Reported cumulative carnivore totals: 0 clones, 8 age deaths, 0 starvation deaths, and 0 fight deaths. This supports investigating failed replacement but does not establish which gate blocked reproduction.

## Implementation
Retain hard stored-energy, health, age, mobility, and cooldown requirements. Replace the hard observable-food gate for both diets with a documented bounded probability that rises gradually with local food per competitor. Make stored energy the primary prerequisite; eligible parents should retain a nonzero breeding chance even under low observed food. Choose and justify the curve, floor, and scale using seeded comparisons. Use central RNG wrappers and local observations only. Evaluate probability once per actual eligible decision, not during diagnostics or repeated eligibility checks. Update domain documentation.

## Validation
Test probability bounds, monotonic response to food and competition, hard eligibility gates, and seeded reproducibility. Compare births by diet, extinction times, and population trajectories across multiple seeds; do not assume guaranteed equilibrium.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adequately provisioned parents are not deterministically barred solely by the former local-food thresholds.
- Food scarcity gradually reduces breeding probability; greater competition does not increase it at equal food.
- Hard energy accounting and age/health/cooldown requirements remain enforced.
- Diagnostics never consume extra RNG draws or change decisions.
- Deterministic tests and multi-seed baseline comparisons document effects on replacement and population growth.
- go test ./..., go test -race ./..., and go vet ./... pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Report reproduction eligibility and blockers by diet
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem
Follow-up to gocreatures-007. The reported run ended near extinction with cumulative carnivore totals of 0 clones and 8 age deaths but no starvation or fight deaths. Current output does not explain why surviving creatures fail to reproduce, and per-tick Clones cannot establish lifetime herbivore reproduction.

## Implementation
Add per-tick and cumulative reproduction diagnostics separately for herbivores and carnivores: evaluated creatures, eligibility, insufficient nutrition, health, age window, cooldown, immobility, and local-food pressure. Distinguish eligible-but-chose-another-action from attempted cloning suppressed during resolution and successful births. If the food gate becomes probabilistic, distinguish probability rejection from hard ineligibility. Document whether blockers overlap or use a primary reason, including denominator and eligibility timing. Evaluate all living decision-makers so higher-priority feeding, escape, or handling does not hide eligibility. Keep accounting inside tick/resolution flow; reuse pure eligibility facts without additional random draws or state changes. Update TickStats, cumulative reporting, report rendering, and CONTEXT.md as appropriate.

## Validation
Use deterministic fixtures for each blocker, multiple simultaneous blockers, action-priority diversion, and combat suppression. Show both per-diet cumulative births and blocker totals in a sample report.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reports distinguish hard ineligibility, local-food/probability suppression, other action selection, resolution suppression, and successful reproduction for each diet.
- Per-tick versus cumulative counters and overlapping versus exclusive blocker semantics are explicit and tested.
- Cumulative herbivore and carnivore births are available; counters reconcile with their documented populations and timing.
- Reporting consumes no randomness and does not change simulation outcomes for a fixed seed.

title: Improve ecological coexistence through food-gated reproduction, predator feeding, and hunger-aware foraging
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Goal
Improve persistent coexistence of plants, herbivores, and carnivores with bounded population cycles. User requested proposal items 1, 3, and 5. These are code-informed hypotheses, not reproduced causes of extinction.

## Scope
1. Food-gated reproduction: require sufficient stored nutrition as well as age and health; explicitly transfer offspring energy from the parent; add a reproduction cooldown (longer for carnivores); reduce reproduction when locally observable food is scarce. Prevent cloning from taking precedence over urgent feeding.
3. Predator meals and handling time: replace the fixed instant kill reward with finite carcass energy related to prey size, multiple feeding actions, digestion/handling time that limits hunting, and carcass decay. Define energy accounting so a kill cannot award both the old reward and a full carcass.
5. Hunger-aware foraging: let critically hungry herbivores seek observed food, weigh hunger against predator avoidance so escape does not indefinitely prevent feeding, and account for competing grazers when choosing destinations. Preserve local observation limits.

## Current behavior and implementation entry points
- actions.go: decideHerbivoreAction and decideCarnivoreAction clone based on age/health without a nutrition gate and before feeding. resolveClone charges parent resources after offspring creation.
- creatures.go: createWithDiet derives offspring nutrition partly from maximum nutrition rather than an explicit parental transfer.
- actions.go: feedCarnivoreOnKill awards 150 nutrition; founder carnivore capacities are 2,000–6,990.
- actions.go: directed herbivore food seeking requires nutrition above 30% and below 70%. decideAction prioritizes any safer escape step over feeding.
- Related contracts: CONTEXT.md, PLANTS.md, herbivore_avoidance.go, tick statistics and reporting.

## Design decisions to settle
Choose and document energy thresholds, cooldowns, local food-availability scoring, prey-to-carcass energy conversion, decay/handling rates, and the hunger-risk tradeoff. Keep parameters explicit and use central RNG wrappers for any stochastic behavior.

## Validation
Use deterministic behavioral tests and multi-seed long-running simulations. Record extinction times, population trajectories, births/deaths by diet, plant growth versus consumption, and predator food intake. Compare against baseline rather than assuming these changes guarantee equilibrium.

## Exclusions
Protected roots/seed banks (item 2) and terrain refuges (item 4) are outside this issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduction requires adequate energy, charges an explicit offspring energy budget, respects cooldowns, and responds to observable food scarcity.
- Predator feeding uses finite carcass resources with decay and handling time; energy is neither duplicated nor consumed twice.
- Critically hungry herbivores pursue known food and can trade safety for feeding; destination scoring accounts for competing grazers.
- Deterministic tests cover energy accounting, cooldown boundaries, carcass depletion/decay, critical-hunger seeking, and hunger versus escape decisions.
- Multi-seed baseline/comparison results document coexistence and extinction behavior without requiring perfectly constant populations.
- Update domain documentation and relevant reporting; go test ./..., go test -race ./..., and go vet ./... pass.
close_reason: Completed food-gated reproduction, finite decaying carcasses with handling time, hunger-aware foraging, deterministic behavioral tests, and five-seed baseline comparison. go test, go test -race, and go vet pass.

title: E: Report plant density, propagation and evolutionary change
description:
## What to build
Expose concise normal-run ecological statistics so slow evolution and resource balance are observable. Report per-species biomass and occupied-cell counts, successful establishments, mutation counts and biomass-weighted trait summaries relative to baselines. Separate per-tick events from cumulative totals and final population snapshots using existing Tick statistics semantics. Include growth versus transfers versus consumption accounting and document the initial parameter table. Avoid a new interactive view; use existing reporting surfaces and a seeded noninteractive diagnostic path where long runs are needed.

## Acceptance criteria
- Per-species biomass and occupied-cell totals agree with the final world snapshot, including mixed cells and extinct species.
- Growth, spread, grazing and mutation events are counted exactly once at their simulation resolution points; failed events do not inflate counts.
- Trait summaries reflect living local populations with sufficient precision to reveal tiny changes; zero-population output is defined.
- Per-tick values reset correctly and cumulative values persist; accounting reconciles biomass across ticks.
- Documented seeded diagnostic runs report plant and creature inheritance/mutation opportunities and realized changes over comparable ticks.

title: F: Validate and tune the integrated textured plant ecosystem
description:
## What to build
Exercise the complete normal simulation and a noninteractive long-run scenario with all slices integrated. Validate resource invariants, deterministic runs, independent species textures under creature overlays, visible propagation fronts, mixed cells and slow local trait drift. Tune the parent baseline parameters only when recorded seeded evidence justifies changes; update the parameter table and explain tradeoffs. This is integration validation, not a substitute for tests in preceding slices. Use runs that can continue ecology observation beyond the normal creature-extinction/lineage stop condition without silently changing interactive stop behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Long runs preserve capacity, nonnegative biomass, bounded traits and accounting; repeat runs with the same seed reproduce world and statistics.
- Terminal review covers every species combination, all density bands and crowded creature/carnivore overlays, with exactly three columns per cell and no frame shimmer.

title: D: Inherit rare bounded plant mutations during colony establishment
description:
## What to build
Add local heritable traits to successful colonization, using the parent evolution model. Founders use species baselines; successful daughter colonies copy the parent cohort and rarely mutate one trait. Do not mutate global species definitions or mutate established populations during ordinary growth. The altered growth/spread/nutritional traits must influence actual simulation outcomes, including grazing value and food-seeking decisions. Keep fixed species identity for visual recognition. Document the one-cohort-per-species-per-cell simplification and extinction/recolonization semantics.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unmutated daughters inherit exact parent traits; an injected deterministic mutation changes at most one eligible trait by at most 0.25% and respects 80–120% bounds.
- Default mutation probability is 0.001 per successful establishment; failed attempts, regrowth and existing-colony rejection cannot mutate traits.
- Traits retain fractional precision, affect growth, spread or feeding as appropriate, and remain local to descendants rather than modifying unrelated colonies.
- Species identity and texture remain stable; fully extinguished local colonies lose their traits and later recolonization inherits the new parent.
- Controlled tests exercise inheritance, mutation boundaries and phenotype effects without flaky probability assertions; seeded sampling documents the rarity relative to creature clone mutations.
- Test/race/vet checks pass and the domain documentation explains plant generations and the intended slower evolutionary timescale.

## Blocked by
gocreatures-bk8.3
acceptance_criteria:
Unmutated daughters inherit exact parent traits; an injected deterministic mutation changes at most one eligible trait by at most 0.25% and respects 80–120% bounds.
Default mutation probability is 0.001 per successful establishment; failed attempts, regrowth and existing-colony rejection cannot mutate traits.
Traits retain fractional precision, affect growth, spread or feeding as appropriate, and remain local to descendants rather than modifying unrelated colonies.
Species identity and texture remain stable; fully extinguished local colonies lose their traits and later recolonization inherits the new parent.
Controlled tests exercise inheritance, mutation boundaries and phenotype effects without flaky probability assertions; seeded sampling documents the rarity relative to creature clone mutations.
Test/race/vet checks pass and the domain documentation explains plant generations and the intended slower evolutionary timescale.

title: A: Feed creatures from a shared-capacity three-species vegetation model
description:
## What to build
Introduce local grass/clover/bramble populations and shared growing capacity as the source of truth. Provide a runnable seeded world with all three species; integrate eating, food observation, movement ranking and tick statistics immediately. Until local propagation lands, retain local regrowth only for populations already present. Establish stable species ordering and read-only biomass/capacity/trait access for independent renderer and propagation work. Store fractional growth/nutrition progress without losing low-rate changes. Use baseline values in the parent epic. Herbivores consume at most five biomass units per action, highest current nutritional yield first with stable species-order ties; account for actual consumed biomass and cap nutrition. Food seeking compares total available nutritional value consistently, with documented conversions for existing thresholds. Carnivores never consume vegetation. Avoid a separately mutable scalar food cache.

## Acceptance criteria
- Running the simulation creates mixed-species populations and herbivores can consume each species using its baseline nutritional yield.
- All populations remain nonnegative and their combined biomass never exceeds shared capacity; zero-capacity and tiny-map cases are defined.
- Observation, movement selection, eating and reporting use the same plant source of truth; obsolete food/maxFood test fixtures are migrated.
- Eating mixed food produces exact biomass-consumed accounting and bounded nutrition, including partial/fractional cases; carnivore behavior remains correct.
- Species identity, local colony, biomass, capacity and nutritional value are documented; renderer/propagation consumers have a stable state contract.
- Deterministic integration tests pass along with go test ./..., go test -race ./... and go vet ./....

## Blocked by
None — can start immediately

Running the simulation creates mixed-species populations and herbivores can consume each species using its baseline nutritional yield.
All populations remain nonnegative and their combined biomass never exceeds shared capacity; zero-capacity and tiny-map cases are defined.
Observation, movement selection, eating and reporting use the same plant source of truth; obsolete food/maxFood test fixtures are migrated.
Eating mixed food produces exact biomass-consumed accounting and bounded nutrition, including partial/fractional cases; carnivore behavior remains correct.

title: B: Render consistent mixed-species textures beneath creatures
description:
## What to build
Render all three species in the normal map using the parent texture contract and the vegetation state delivered by A. Use stable three-column species positions to expose minority populations; reserve background identity/density under creature glyphs and draw texture only in unoccupied foreground positions. Use narrow, terminal-safe texture primitives with a documented ASCII fallback if needed. Provide a compact legend explaining species, density bands and the limitation that creature overlays hide foreground texture. No vegetation-view toggle. Keep rendering deterministic and independent from simulation RNG.

## Acceptance criteria
- Empty, sparse, medium and dense examples visibly progress from dark soil to richer species texture/background; each positive density band is documented.

title: C: Grow seeded plant patches through snapshot-based local propagation
description:
## What to build
Replace independent random food placement/regrowth with seeded patches, density-limited regrowth, species-specific local dispersal and shared-capacity competition using the parent starting parameters. Collect growth/spread intents from the tick-start plant snapshot, resolve them, then apply once before creature decisions. Prevent scan-direction cascades; define stable tie arbitration without permanent species priority and isolate random draws from traversal order. Existing same-species colonies reject colonization; other species may coexist. Establishment transfers parent biomass, so distinguish growth-created biomass from spread transfers in statistics. Seeded patch initialization must handle overlaps, boundaries and small maps explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria
- With a controlled seed, grass expands cardinally, clover into eight-neighbor gaps, and bramble within distance two; no new colony can spread again in its birth tick.
- An isolated empty region receives no plants without a reachable parent; a completely extinct species does not spontaneously reappear.
- Eligibility thresholds, attempt rates, target selection, establishment transfer and fractional density-limited regrowth match documented configuration.
- Simultaneous competing intents never exceed source biomass or destination capacity, do not always favor one species, and preserve multi-species cells where space exists.
- Seeded outcomes are repeatable; reversing candidate enumeration after stable event ordering produces equivalent plant updates.
- Growth, grazing and biomass-transfer accounting reconcile across ticks; long-run boundedness and edge/corner tests pass with test/race/vet checks.

title: Plant ecology: textured mixed vegetation and slow evolution
description:
## What to build
Deliver grass, clover and bramble with consistent density textures, mixed-species cells, creature-over-plant layering, local propagation and slow heritable evolution. All slices are AFK (implementable without a required human decision); manually inspect terminal output as part of visual verification. No vegetation-view toggle initially.

Starting design: three stable species positions in each existing three-column map cell. Species identity uses both texture and color: grass olive vertical texture; clover teal stipple; bramble muted-purple crosshatch. Texture primitives are terminal characters, not species-letter/icon labels. Dark soil at zero; positive density bands 1–9%, 10–39%, 40–69%, 70–100% of shared cell capacity, with increasing texture weight and background intensity. Each species retains its position even at low density. Creature foreground takes precedence; species backgrounds remain underneath.

Initial tuning values (explicit starting points, subject to seeded evidence): shared capacity 100 biomass units/cell; grass/clover/bramble intrinsic regrowth 0.08/0.04/0.02 biomass units per tick, nutrition 15/20/10 per consumed biomass unit, spread eligibility 20/30/40 local biomass, attempt probability 0.02/0.01/0.005 per eligible colony per tick. Grass targets cardinal neighbors, clover all eight adjacent neighbors, bramble offsets within Chebyshev distance two. One target per attempt, uniform among the species offsets; reject out-of-bounds, insufficient space, or existing same-species colonies. Successful establishment transfers one biomass unit from parent to target. No spontaneous reappearance after initialization. Grow existing populations with rate multiplied by free-capacity fraction, retaining fractional progress; allocate contested space without fixed species priority. Initial patches: per species max(1, ceil(cellCount/300)) centers, each with 20 biomass and adjacent halo cells with 5, within shared capacity; document small-map behavior.

Evolution: one local cohort per species per cell, inherited on successful colonization of a cell lacking that species. Existing same-species colonies are not overwritten or averaged by arriving propagules. Founders have base traits. A successful establishment has 0.1% mutation probability; at most one of regrowth rate, spread probability, or nutritional yield changes by up to ±0.25% relative, bounded to 80–120% of the species base. Preserve fractional traits so tiny changes are meaningful. Species identity, texture, spread neighborhood and threshold remain fixed initially. No mutation on tick entry, failed spread or ordinary regrowth. Compare documented per-establishment mutation rate and magnitude with current creature cloning (typically ±1% changes on each clone); quantify realized rates in seeded runs rather than promise a wall-clock timescale.

Dependency waves: A foundation -> B textures and C propagation in parallel -> D evolution after C (can overlap B) -> E ecology reporting after D (can overlap B) -> F integrated validation after B and E. Shared integration points may require merge coordination even where logical dependencies permit parallel work. Each slice updates domain documentation and includes its own meaningful tests; final validation covers cross-slice behavior. Use central RNG wrappers, snapshot/resolve plant updates, and keep mutation out of creature decision goroutines.

## Acceptance criteria
- All six child slices are delivered with recorded validation evidence.
- Normal map shows three plant species and their individual density cues, including mixed cells and creature overlays.
- Plants spread locally, compete for bounded capacity, feed creatures and transmit slowly evolving local traits.
- Domain terms, initial settings, evolution semantics, texture legend and dependency ordering are documented.
